newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end lower, led by gold.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end lower, led by gold.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures ended lower across the board Wednesday, but volumes were light apart from in COMEX gold trading.
"We view all four precious metals with negative bias," Merrill Lynch senior analyst Bill O'Neill said.
"Our $300 downside objective for gold is probably conservative and $3.80 is not an unreasonable objective for silver," he said.

After hitting an 11-day high last Friday, gold prices slipped lower again late Tuesday and Wednesday, on talk of European central bank selling around $330.00, and on news South Africa's Western Areas Gold Mining Co Ltd said it had completed a buy back of 1.6 million ounces of a 7.3 million ounce forward sale arranged in 1995.
Comments by U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Greenspan late Tuesday, also helped push the U.S. dollar and stock and bond markets sharply higher, pressuring gold prices lower Wednesday.

Greenspans said U.S. economic growth was slowing, inflation in 1997 was modest, and the falling gold price reflected a lowering of inflation expectations, all of which meant a near term monetary policy tightening could be avoided.
COMEX August gold ended down $2.20 at $323.80 an ounce, after support at $325.00 gave way during the session.
The August/December spread narrowed further to $2.90 an ounce, as funds rolled short positions into the December contract, traders said.
Estimated total COMEX gold volume was again heavy at 66,000 lots Wednesday.
COMEX gold open interest fell 7,865 lots Tuesday to 204,621 contracts, declining from an 18 month high at 222,069 contracts on July 16.
In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted around $322.75/25, compared to the London Wednesday afternoon fix at $324.90, and the New York close Tuesday around $325.30/80.
Meanwhile, COMEX September silver ended down 0.80 cents at $4.295 an ounce, with support seen around $4.20 and resistance around $4.40, after the contract saw a contract low at $4.145 last week.
The September/December spread narrowed further to 6.00 cents an ounce. Estimated total COMEX silver volume was a moderate 13,000 lots.
NYMEX October platinum slipped $1.00 to end at $408.20, giving back some of Tuesday's sharp gains, while NYMEX September palladium ended off just 50 cents at $179.50 an ounce.
"Platinum and palladium are still experiencing some physical tightness, but Russian supplies are gradually moving into the pipeline and we see lower prices later this summer," Merrill's O'Neill said.
"However, shorts should probably still be avoided."

Platinum group metals prices (PGMs) climbed further on the Tokyo Commodity Exchange (TOCOM) Tuesday, as the dollar rose against the yen, and the spot palladium price climbed back over $200.00 for the first time since early June.
But refining sources said the Russians were offering palladium in the spot market in Europe and some deals were done which caused prices to ease.
The forward curve remains highly backwardated though and lease rates for one month palladium sponge remain over 100 pct though, traders said.
Russian shipments of palladium to Japan resumed last week, with the arrival of palladium, but no platinum arrivals have yet been reported.
